case_title: Ohan Raj @ Dhand v. State of Haryana
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.341 and s.392 r/w s.397
confession: Extra judicial confession of co-accused, but not relied on
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleged that the deceased, a doctor, was murdered and his belongings were taken. The deceased's body was found in a field with injuries from a sharp-edged weapon. The accused were linked to the crime through the recovery of stolen items and statements from a co-accused. The co-accused initially named different accomplices in two confessional statements, creating inconsistencies. The recovery of items was questioned as they were common and not of significant value. There was no direct evidence placing the accused at the scene of the crime, and the presence of the accused near the crime scene was not corroborated by independent evidence.
